compiled_state.description:
# Coaching move: when a plan stops CONVERGING, propose a decomposition instead of another finding list

## The observation

Twice in epic e369 a plan absorbed round after round of review findings, and both times the
remedy was not a better answer to the findings — it was **splitting the ticket**:

* **J9 [rebar:bda8-370d-23ad-4e36]** blocked EIGHT times. Extracting the exception contract into
  J10 [rebar:bb8c...] produced a first-try PASS.
* **b586 [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260]** has now taken TEN rounds and is still BLOCK. Its findings
  partition cleanly into two concerns that alternate: the POLICY (rounds 1, 4, 8, 9, 10 — helper
  reuse, duplicate-risk scoping, citation precision, the per-call read/mutation boundary, what
  exception escapes at cap exhaustion) and the MECHANICS of the module extraction the 800-LOC cap
  forces (rounds 6, 7 — what moves, what routes through what, which tree the LOC is measured on).
  Each fix in one concern re-opened surface in the other.

The gate is doing its job in both cases — the findings were real and several were serious. What it
cannot currently say is the thing a senior reviewer would say on round four: *"stop answering these
one at a time; this is two tickets."*

## Why the obvious trigger is WRONG

"After N rounds, suggest splitting" would have fired on b586 at round 3 and been wrong. Rounds 1
through 9 CONVERGED — 20 advisory + 1 blocking, down to 1 blocking. That is a plan being iterated
well, and telling its author to restructure would have been noise that trains people to ignore the
gate.

**The signal is not the round count. It is the loss of convergence**, and it has a specific shape:

1. **Non-monotonicity** — the blocking count RISES after having fallen (b586: 1 blocking at round 9,
   7+ at round 10). That is the fingerprint of "fixing one thing re-opened another."
2. **Alternating clusters** — findings partition into >= 2 groups by criteria code and cited
   location, and consecutive rounds hit DIFFERENT groups rather than drilling into one.
3. **Disjoint citation sets** — the groups cite non-overlapping files/sections (b586: the extraction
   findings cite `transport.py` structure; the policy findings cite `_errors` / `dispatch_one`
   semantics).

Requiring all three is what keeps it from firing on a plan that is simply deep.

## The move itself

When those conditions hold, the gate stops emitting an (N+1)th finding list and instead emits a
**structural verdict**: the cluster partition it actually computed, round-by-round, plus a proposed
decomposition — "these 10 rounds' findings fall into 2 groups that alternate; here are the 2
candidate tickets, and here is which findings belong to each."

Design constraints that matter:

* **Advisory, not a new blocking verdict.** Keeping one ticket is a legitimate authorial choice; the
  gate should make the structural claim VISIBLE, not enforce it. It also must not become a way to
  dodge findings — the findings still stand and still block.
* **It must show its work.** The value is in the partition, not the recommendation. An author who
  disagrees needs the round-by-round cluster assignment to argue with, exactly as they would with a
  finding's evidence.
* **No new storage.** `rebar audit show <id>`'s `plan_reviews` array already retains the per-round
  `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars — verified: b586 currently carries 10 retained rounds. The trend is
  computable from what is already there.
* **Prefer deterministic clustering first.** Findings already carry structured `criteria` and
  `location` fields, so grouping may not need an LLM call at all. Reach for a model only if the
  deterministic partition proves too coarse.

## The confound to handle honestly

b586's description grew from ~8.8 KB to ~28 KB across the ten rounds. **More plan is more surface,
so some of the rising finding count is the plan getting longer, not worse.** Any trend metric should
normalize by plan size (or at minimum surface the size delta alongside the count) — otherwise the
move will fire on thorough authors, which is precisely the population it should leave alone.

## Open questions (this is an idea, not a design)

* Do the retained `plan_reviews` sidecars expose per-round BLOCKING COUNTS? The projection checked
  here showed the verdicts but not the counts, so the trend's raw input needs confirming before any
  of this is buildable.
* Where should it surface — in the `review-plan` output, in `review-plan --status`, or only in
  `rebar audit show`? The first is loudest and the most likely to be resented.
* Should it ever fire at round 1 on a plan that is obviously two tickets (e.g. one whose Scope lists
  two unrelated modules and whose ACs partition with them)? That is a different, cheaper detector
  and possibly the better first version.
* J9's split was authored by a human noticing the pattern. Is one automated nudge enough to change
  behaviour, or does the coaching only work when it names the CANDIDATE SPLIT concretely?

## PRIOR ART — this is a MOVE in an existing registry, not a new mechanism

Checked before leaving this as an idea, and it substantially shrinks the scope. rebar already has a
**Pass-4 coach with a pluggable move-registry**:

* [rebar:cf40-f372-47a1-44a3] (closed) extracted the coach MECHANISM into the kernel and defined a
  registered move-registry SCHEMA `{id, name, template, triggers/applies_when}`, with selection as a
  DETERMINISTIC filter on `triggers` and only then an LLM choice among the applicable moves. Each
  gate supplies its own catalog.
* [rebar:315d-b4ba-6c9e-482d], [rebar:75a9-01c2-304d-4532], [rebar:5dac-c177-56ff-4af4] and
  [rebar:e3cf-3afc-e80d-4d19] are prior moves shipped through that machinery.

So the deliverable is most likely **one registry entry plus its `triggers` predicate**, not new
plumbing — and the "prefer deterministic clustering first" note above is already the house pattern
rather than a novel suggestion.

**THE ONE REAL MECHANISM GAP, and it is the crux of this idea.** The existing coach operates on the
SURVIVING ADVISORIES OF A SINGLE PASS. This move's trigger is inherently CROSS-ROUND — it needs the
previous rounds' blocking counts and cluster assignments, which a per-pass coach does not have in
hand. So the honest scoping is:

* if the coach can be given read access to the retained `plan_reviews` sidecars, this is a normal
  registry entry with an unusual `triggers` predicate;
* if it cannot, the mechanism needs a cross-round input FIRST, and that — not the move — is the
  actual piece of work. Settle this before estimating.

## RELATIONSHIP TO [rebar:259c-0f29-e920-4fab] — adjacent, NOT a duplicate

259c is an advisory nudge that fires on a LEAF WHOSE ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA COUNT is high, because
completion-verification effort is linear in criteria count. Both coach "this ticket may be too big",
so they should be read together and their messages must not collide. They differ in the signal:

* 259c is STATIC and fires on ROUND ONE from the plan's own shape (criteria count).
* this one is DYNAMIC and cannot fire before round three, because it needs a TREND.

259c is the cheaper detector and probably the better first version of the family — which is also the
answer to one of the open questions above. If only one of the two is built, build 259c.

## Provenance

Both instances are recorded in session log [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9] (handoff #4 lesson 3, and
handoff #7). The b586 round-by-round breakdown that this generalises from is a comment on
[rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260].
compiled_state.title: Plan-review coaching move: when findings stop converging, propose a decomposition
